house.description: Employers required to disclose in job postings whether employee health plan options comply with cost-sharing limits.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Workforce, Labor, and Economic Development Finance and Policy

latest_action.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Workforce, Labor, and Economic Development Finance and Policy

bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to employment; requiring employers to disclose in job postings whether employee health plan options comply with cost-sharing limits; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 181.173, subdivision 2.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 181.173, subdivision 2, is amended to read:

Subd. 2.
Salary ranges in job postings required.
(a) An employer must disclose in each posting for each job opening with the employer the starting salary range, and a general description of all of the benefits and other compensation, including but not limited to any health or retirement benefits, to be offered to a hired job applicant[+, as well as whether a hired job applicant will be offered a health plan option that complies with the cost-sharing limits under section 62Q.481, subdivision 1+].
(b) An employer that does not plan to offer a salary range for a position must list a fixed pay rate. A salary range may not be open ended.
